lens: all three in turn (learning-scientist, examiner, learner-advocate); criterion scores are the mean of the three lens readings
scope_note: Teaching quality only; no factual checking (knowledge-only mode). Read module.json by sections: S1 and S2 in full, S3 in full, S4 in full, S5.emerg to S5.child, the end-of-file report (traps, error_types, calibration, help, pace, next_steps) and the cold-probe cards; the S5 tail and S6 probe nodes were NOT read node by node, so S6 is judged from the sim walks and cold-probe structure. Read sim/novice.md and all four sim/*.report.json. Gate checks were applied to every node read; no dead end or unreachable branch was seen. Note: the earlier review.json (judge m1) describes several hints as 'Try again only' and some 'Show me why' routes as going to the next probe; in the current module.json these are not true for S4.a_hint, S4.b_hint, S4.d1_hint, S4.d3_hint, S4.e1/e2 hints, S4.f_hint, S5.emerg_hint or S5.taxis_why_hint (each has Show me why, kind agency), nor for S2.tri_t2a, S2.tri_t2b or S2.conj_t28a (Show me why goes to S2.tri_ok or S2.conj_ok). Those m1 flaws were not carried over.

segments.reason: Real exam stem as the hook with confidence tick; TR1 re-tested in a position-statement form (S1.retest_route); qualifier trap TR5 in S1.tim_probe. Weak point: the femoral option in S1.hook is easy to exclude by the stem's vessel framing.

Thin trap work in the boundary block: S2.tri_probe2 has only two real options (no third distractor), S2.tri_t2b is a one-line verdict with no tempting-why, and S2.tri_help removes two of three options so the hint nearly gives the key. Good: S2.route_predict, S2.pic_probe and S2.cause_predict tie cause and descent to the right sac.

Predict-then-show on the occlusion test (S3.occl_v) and the laparoscopic route (S3.lap, TR1 in clinical form); Zieman and TR31 probes are well built. Weak: S3.lap has two options, S3.wall2 re-asks the S3.wall fact one node later, and S3.contrast bundles three claims per option.

Form tells break DP1: in S4.a_probe the key 'Femoral hernia' is the only option without 'inguinal' (the two traps both say inguinal), and S4.f_probe repeats the tell. Dominated distractors: S4.c1_probe 'Umbilical' and S4.f 'Strangulated direct' are excluded by any learner who knows the stem. S4.c1, S4.d4, S4.e1 and S4.e2 offer no hint button. Strong: S4.b_probe (narrow neck versus bulk, both bulk traps tempting), S4.d3 and S4.e1 feedback.

Best refutation writing in the module: S5.emerg_t11 and S5.taxis_why_t1 name the wrong model then refute it with claims; S5.adult pairs the older PYQ key and the current standard. Weak: S5.child key is the only option that does not use the 'Excise the sac, then ...' frame, so it is findable by form; S5.emerg restates S4.d1 almost word for word; S5.taxis_why repeats the same stem; S5.ex2 packs four steps into one stem.

Cold probes and fresh-form retests are present (12 cold probes), but the consolidate run is long and padded (sim walks of 215 steps for the novice), several retests repeat earlier stems, and the report's sliding-hernia claim in O6 is not taught in any node. Judged from sim notes and structure; S6 nodes not read one by one.

best_parts: node S1.hook: real exam stem, confidence tick, and the two traps (TR1 direct, TR40 femoral) are each a named wrong model; the retest S1.retest_route re-asks TR1 in a position-statement form.
node S3.occl_v: predict-then-show on the occlusion test with a femoral trap (TR40), an indirect trap (TR21) and the direct key; the hint asks which door the finger shuts without giving the answer.

node S5.child_t1 and S5.taxis_why_t1: 'Tempting: ...' then refutation with claims, then 'Show me the answer' to an explanation node. This is the feedback pattern to copy into S2.tri_t2b and S2.conj_t28a.
node S4.b_probe: both bulk-based traps (TR8) are plausible to a learner who judges risk by size, and the key is the neck.
report traps block: each trap text has avoided, fell_recovered and fell_open variants, and fell_open names the repair (predict-then-show or contrast) in plain words.
flaws: node S4.a_probe: the key 'Femoral hernia' is the only option without 'inguinal'; both traps say 'inguinal', so the key is findable by form (DP1).
node S4.f_probe: same form tell as S4.a_probe, with both traps saying 'inguinal' and the key saying 'femoral'.
node S4.c1_probe: 'Umbilical hernia' is dominated for anyone who knows the stem, and the probe has no hint and no 'Not sure' option (DP2, R5).
node S5.child: key is the only option without the 'Excise the sac, then ...' frame (DP1); the two TR7 traps share it.
node S2.tri_probe2: two real options plus a hint, with no third distractor for the medial border; the planned conjoint-tendon distractor is absent.
node S2.tri_t2b: 'The deep ring is not the triangle's lower edge' gives a verdict with no why-tempting and no refutation (R2).

node S5.emerg and S4.d1_probe: near-identical stem and key ('tense, tender ... resuscitate, then emergency surgery') within about 30 nodes; a repeat in the same form, not a retest in a new form (R6, R3 pace).
node S5.taxis_why and S4.d2 mechanism probe: the same 'why is forceful reduction avoided' stem recurs; recast one as a case.
report O6 gap text: 'a left sliding hernia most often contains sigmoid colon' teaches sliding contents, which no node teaches or tests; O6 lists sliding in its objective text.

report calibration.overconfident: says 'review the confident errors first', but the card_order for the misconceived persona is the default 0 to 11, so the stated order is not applied and the trap cards do not mark which errors were sure.

novice.note: Headline weak, gap and shaky texts match the path (hinted_only O1, cold 4 of 12), trap fell_open texts name the wrong model and repair, next steps are clear. Sim friction (feedback ending in a question with no answer slot in S5.emerg_t12, S5.nerve_t1, S5.adult_t1, S5.adult_t2) is a node defect, not a report defect.

misconceived.note: Overconfident calibration and the 20 confident errors are stated correctly, but the card order is unchanged from the default, and the 'confident errors first' instruction is not what the learner gets. Trap texts do not say 'you were sure' for the confident errors.

strong.note: Strong headline, calibrated line and all-avoided traps are accurate. The fast-lane text correctly says skipping means the cards should be checked. The strong persona gets no unnecessary repair.

guesser.note: The current file's guesser report describes the path accurately: sure_wrong 14, guess_right 6, hints 24, fast lane taken, and confident errors marked. The weakness is that the guesser's skipped S4.a lesson gets the generic fast-lane text, which does not name the skipped lesson or its cards, so the learner is not sent to the right cards.

rank_note: Single module, no ranking. Round 1 scores 3.52 weighted; the refine threshold is 4.0. Priority rebuild: S4 (form tells, dominated distractors, cold probes without hints), then S2 (thin boundary distractors and one-line feedback), then S6 (padding and repeated stems).
merge_ideas: S2.tri_t2b and S2.conj_t28a take the S5.child_t1 'Tempting: X, then refute' pattern, and 'Show me why' goes to an explanation node (already true) rather than the next probe.
S4.a_probe and S4.f_probe: put 'groin' or 'inguinal' in the femoral key and in one trap, so the scope word is not the only differing token.
S5.child: rewrite all three options in the same 'Excise ...' frame with one differing clause.
Every probe with no hint (S4.c1, S4.d4, S4.e1, S4.e2) gets a hint and a 'Not sure' option, so the hint ladder holds on every key probe.
S4.d1_probe and S5.emerg: keep the strangulation stem once in S4 and recast S5.emerg as a case with a different vignette (say an older woman with a femoral lump) so the re-test is a new form.
Report: confident-error trap cards get a 'you were sure' marker and come first in card_order, so the 'confident errors first' instruction is true for the misconceived persona.
